claims.text: Products classified as healthy were purchased more frequently during the olfactory condition compared to the control condition.
Products classified as healthy were purchased more frequently during the olfactory condition compared to the visual condition.
Purchases of products classified as healthy during the visual condition did not differ significantly from the control condition.
Higher product prices were associated with lower odds of purchasing a product classified as healthy.
Time of day was not significantly associated with purchasing choices of healthy versus non-healthy products.

evidence.description: Among N = 1043 purchases, products classified as healthy were more frequent during the olfactory week than during the control week.
Among N = 1043 purchases, products classified as healthy were more frequent during the olfactory week than during the visual week.
The visual condition did not differ significantly from control.
Higher prices were associated with lower odds of purchasing a product classified as healthy in binary logistic regression analysis.
Time of day was not significantly associated with purchasing behavior in the logistic regression model.

methodologies.name: Quasi-experimental field sensory nudging intervention
methodologies.description: Field study tracking university vending machine purchases across three consecutive one-week sensory cue conditions, analyzed with binary logistic regression incorporating price and time of day.

limitations.text: Much of existing evidence on sensory cues and food choice is derived from laboratory studies, leaving everyday settings underexplored.
The study relied on a quasi-experimental consecutive-week design rather than a randomized or counterbalanced design.
The intervention was conducted only within a university vending-machine environment, limiting generalizability across diverse real-world food-choice settings.

future_work.text: Confirming the sensory nudging findings using randomized or counterbalanced experimental designs.
Replicating sensory cue interventions across diverse real-world food-choice settings beyond university contexts.
